onboarding.title: Setting up Pip
onboarding.saveFailed: Pip could not save that. Try again.

welcome.title: Hi, I'm Pip.
welcome.body: I help you read work messages, especially when something changes. First, let's set me up for you. Here is what we will do:
list: Pick your language, how much movement you want and how I talk to you
See how I keep your messages private
Tell me who you work with
Answer 6 short questions about how you work best
Learn about energy faces and do your first check-in
Try me on a practice message
welcome.time: It takes about 5 minutes. You can skip any step, or stop and come back later.

comfort.title: Language, movement and how I talk
comfort.body: Choose these first, so the rest of setup feels right. You can change them any time in Settings.
comfort.motionNote: Pip and the cards move less. Your system's reduce-motion setting already does this.

privacy.title: What I see, and what I never see
rules: I only read text you select and send me with the shortcut, and what you type or dictate to me and send. I never read your email or chat by myself.
Before anything leaves your computer, I swap names for roles and remove emails, phone numbers and links. Notes you keep go out again this way with later messages.
I never send anything for you. You copy what you want.

spoons.title: Energy faces
spoons.body: Pip's check-ins are inspired by spoon theory, where many autistic people count their energy in spoons. Instead of counting spoons, you pick a face: 1 is a very tired face, 5 is a bright one. Tap the one that fits, no explaining needed. When your face is a tired one, I show fewer steps and say what can wait.
